描述_ZN: Painting of a bamboo fan, Ming Dynasty, 1633, painted by Ni Yuanlu on gold paper and ink, 17.6 cm long and 52.1 cm wide.　　Ni Yuanlu was known for his calligraphy, but his paintings are rarely seen in the world. This small fan is painted with ink strokes of bamboo, with a few strokes, sparse and dense, different in intensity and shade, with a casual and vivid attitude. Bamboo was given the symbolic meaning of modesty and nobility by ancient literati, and became a traditional subject of literati painting with anthropomorphic images. Ni Yuanlu, who was straightforward in nature, was a man of the time, and eventually died for the Ming Dynasty, so bamboo is indeed a reflection of his life.　　This painting is signed: "In the summer of Kueiyou, Yuanlu resembled Bingli zhang", and inscribed with a white square seal of "Yuanlu's playful brushwork". Kueiyou is the sixth year of Chongzhen of the Ming Dynasty (1633), when Ni Yuanlu was 41 years old. There is an inscription on the edge of the frame by Zhao Yannong, a modernist.
